title: Choose FounderHub's visual world
question: The roll assigned Line Map. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Line Map
options.lineage: Bay Area transit system maps and station wayfinding
options.thesis: Every hypothesis is a line; every quote is a stop on its way to a score.
options.viewport: Navy sign-band header with standard tabs; the hypothesis set like a station name; a route strip runs from the 50% start through each quote as a stop to the current score; Supports and Disproves columns below.
options.risk: If the route strip is drawn timidly it reads as a plain timeline, and the world shrinks to a colour scheme.

raised.raise: Contested hypotheses fork their line, so conflict reads in the drawing itself, not only in red versus green.
One type family carries everything from station name to caption; 1px hairlines replace card boxes and shadows.
The hypothesis board packs every hypothesis edge to edge in whole cells instead of airy cards.
Every dimension snaps to one 8px module; nothing sits off the grid.
Length is exact quantity: each stop's segment on the route is proportional to that quote's weight.

options.label: Evidence Cards
options.lineage: policy debate evidence cards and the flowsheet
options.thesis: Every quote is cut like a debate card: tag, cite, and the highlighted words that count.
options.viewport: The hypothesis as the tag line, then Aff and Neg columns of cards with the extracted quote highlighted inside its surrounding context.
options.risk: The most familiar fit for 'quotes first'; the highlighter can read as a study app.

options.label: Centre Rail
options.thesis: Supports and Disproves set as twin columns around a centre rail of source keys.
materials: hairline rules at one device pixel
options.viewport: Twin quote columns around a narrow vermilion rail; score and apparatus hang in the wide margin.
options.case: Holds product clarity: for and against become the page's own symmetry. Loses on audience: reads as a scholarly edition.
options.risk: Lands squarely in the 'too academic' you ruled out.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Evidence as overlapping translucent sheets with hatch densities.
options.viewport: Stacked sheets over a zone ramp.
options.risk: Founders do not live in darkrooms.
options.case: Loses both axes: no audience tie, and hatch density hides the quotes.
options.kept: Conflict drawn structurally: contested lines fork.

options.label: Design Annual
options.thesis: Each hypothesis as a registered plate on uncoated stock.
options.risk: A showcase, not a working tool.
options.case: Loses both axes: gallery framing slows reading evidence.
options.kept: One type family throughout; hairlines instead of boxes.

options.label: Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Every source as a stamp-sized cell in a packed grid.
options.viewport: Hundreds of cells on one page.
options.case: Loses both axes: density without legible quotes.
options.kept: Density courage: the board packs whole cells edge to edge.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Scores built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.risk: Display type fights a working screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: poster logic, no founder tie.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: For and against as mirrored columns, time read upward.
options.viewport: A vertical staff with flanking columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: notation founders cannot read.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean research dashboard in the Linear and Vercel register, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, header with score, two quote columns in bordered panels.
canonCard.risk: This is the generic SaaS look you ruled out, by design.
